checks.check: Each D102 metadata SELECT uses PreparedStatement with queryTimeout 20 seconds, finite maxRows and fetchSize. VIEW/source state limits are 2, preserving absent/duplicate detection; full source schema limit is 18, which exceeds each admitted 6/11-column schema and preserves exact schema rejection.

The wrapper changes JDBC statement construction only. Original VIEW SQL/token/status/directory checks, both fixed source metadata vectors, strict non-null counters/WAL settlement, exact source schemas and complete DEDUP keys remain intact.

Private and formal acceptance both construct JdbcTemplate through jdbc(pool).setQueryTimeout(20), so plain snapshot, count and independent VIEW reads inherit the timeout; explicitly bounded aggregate/reader statements retain their own limits.
The earlier evidence fix remains: after is computed once, compared with before, and the same value is persisted as metadata_after.

New guard test actually invokes each PreparedStatementCreator against mocked Connection and verifies the timeout/maxRows/fetchSize; it covers 12 metadata statements across both before/after captures and disallows raw String/ResultSetExtractor metadata calls.

caveats: 20 seconds is a per-statement JDBC query timeout, not an overall 20-second operation deadline or proof that a 30-second ReadGroup request interrupts in-flight JDBC work. A page performs multiple sequential guarded SELECTs; pool connection acquisition is governed separately.

The previous scope limits remain: daily bounds limit output buckets rather than proving native raw JOIN scan cardinality; no provider universe readiness or cutover certification; D102 live reuses D101's actual source increment rather than causing source revision itself.
This review does not execute or certify the new 24th test, private schema audit or live acceptance. The coordinator will run them sequentially and decides admission.
